Commentary.Commentary: So Williamson has been handed the trophy and he, along with his team, poses with it. End of a hard-fought series. We bid you goodbye from this one but there is plenty of cricketing action going on. You can catch the ongoing Australia-India Test in Adelaide with Day 3 to begin on Saturday at 1030 local (0000 GMT). Cheers!

New Zealand skipper and Man of the Match, Kane Williamson, says it was a fantastic performance, especially as Pakistan are strong in their backyard. Adds that it's special to win the decider and his team will remember this for a long time. Mentions that they knew it would be hard work to do well here, but they stayed positive despite the ebbs and flows and didn't get ahead of themselves which helped. Reckons that they didn't let themselves fall behind at any stage which helped them put pressure on Pakistan. On his spinners, he says they showed their talent and experience and it's a big deal to perform after coming to such a place. Further adds that besides his performance, Henry Nicholls and the others buckled down and put in key performances which proved to be the difference in the end. Before he's done, Kane congratulates Mohammad Hafeez for a wonderful career and wishes him the best of luck in his future endeavours.

Pakistan captain, Sarfraz Ahmed, says they were the ones who let the opportunities slide, especially as a batting unit, which cost them the series. Mentions that the tailenders aren't able to contribute either which is adding to their batting woes. Continues saying that it's been 4-5 matches where they have collapsed like this on the final day of the Test and they need to work on that. On their tour to South Africa, states that they have to be positive over there and be mentally strong for the challenge.

Man of the Series, Yasir Shah, thanks the Almighty first up. Says that after a good while he's performed well in a series, so is happy to get the award. Informs that he used to work hard in the nets and even improved his action after studying a lot of videos. Stresses that he gives his best every time he steps out on the pitch, but expresses his disappointment at not winning the series.

Two sessions is all it took for the Black Caps to bundle the Pakistan batsmen out. Five were taken before Lunch and five post Lunch. Southee, Ajaz and Somerville all took 3 apiece but one would say, it was the debutant who was the tormentor-in-chief as his three were probably the wickets which would have hurt Pakistan the most.

Quick runs this morning, from Colin de Grandhomme, Tim Southee and Henry Nicholls, who remained unbeaten, saw the Kiwis bat Pakistan out of the game. Also, that helped Williamson declare much earlier than what one would have expected and the visitors set a target of 280.

New Zealand then trailed by 74 and even before they had cut down the deficit, they were 4 down. Then though came the recovery. A magnificent 212-run stand between skipper Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls took New Zealand into a commanding position heading into Day 5. The former got to his ton on Day 4, whereas the latter did the same on Day 5.

Then with the bat too, the hosts were in an excellent position to take a big first innings lead when Azhar Ali and Asad Shafiq were batting. The two added a 201-run stand with both scoring tons and Pakistan were cruising at 286/4, but a collapse then saw them being bundled out for 348. Somerville was the star, as the debutant finished with the 4-fer, hence keeping the home side in check.

Pakistan, however, had their moments but failed to capitalize on it. They had New Zealand on the mat at 72/4 in the first innings, but let them off the hook as Williamson and Watling added a brilliant 104-run stand. Both scored half centuries and took New Zealand to a respectable total.

A huge achievement for the Kiwis. They have managed to beat Pakistan in their fortress. What an effort from them, one they would remember for a long, long time. A team effort is what it was and not many would have given them a chance heading into the third and final Test, especially after the battering they got in the second game. They have bounced back extremely well and taken the series 2-1.

OUT! And there it is! A famous series win in the U.A.E. for New Zealand. What a tremendous effort. Smiles and handshakes all around, they'll be mighty proud of it. It's floated up by Patel, Hasan Ali comes down the track to go big but ends up getting a big top edge. It balloons towards point where fittingly, skipper Kane Williamson takes the catch. NEW ZEALAND WIN BY 123 RUNS AND TAKE THE SERIES 2-1!

We are back for what could probably be the last session. The skipper Sarfraz Ahmed joins Babar Azam in the middle. Ajaz Patel will bowl the remaining two balls of his over. Here we go...
... Final Day, Afternoon Session ...

A session which has thoroughly belonged to New Zealand. In 29.4 overs in this session, 136 runs were scored for the loss of 8 wickets. Pakistan have only scored 55 of them and the 5 wickets lost are theirs, so you picture it for yourself. After de Grandhomme and Nicholls put on the quick runs, the Kiwis declared early to have a go at Pakistan and that decision has paid dividends as the hosts have lost 5 wickets already. Hafeez, who is playing his last Test, the two centurions from the first innings, Haris and Imam, all have been sent back. Barring Boult, everyone has chipped in with the wickets and turned the pressure on Pakistan. The next session could just be the last one. Join us on the other side of the break to find out.

An appeal follows, not a confident one by the bowler but Watling is very sure about it. The umpire shakes his head. Watling wants it to be reviewed and Williamson does so. Ultra Edge shows that there is a spike as the ball passes the glove. The on-field call has to be overturned. New Zealand now 6 wickets away with around 61 overs to go. Somerville is on a hat-trick here.
Review time. It's for a caught behind appeal against Asad Shafiq. Is he gone? Seems unlikely to the naked eye, but you never know...
Asad Shafiq is the new man in.

Good length delivery outside off, Sohail lets it go.
Again wide outside off, Sohail shoulders his arms to this one.
Bowls wide outside off, the left-hander offers no shot.
Length delivery on off, Sohail defends off the front foot.
NO BALL! De Grandhomme oversteps. Good length delivery on off, Sohail defends off the back foot.
Bowls a bouncer, the left-hander ducks underneath it.
Bowls short of length delivery, Imam defends off the back foot.
Bowls a bouncer, Imam does well to duck under it.
Again on a good length on off, the left-hander defends off the back foot.
Good length delivery on off, Imam defends off the back foot.
Bowls a bouncer, Imam had less time to react to duck under it.
Good length delivery outside off, the left-hander lets it go.
Third consecutive leave for Haris Sohail. Wide outside off, Sohail offers no shot.
Wide outside off, Sohail offers no shot.
Wide outside off, the left-hander shoulders his arms to this one.
Good length delivery on middle, the left-hander keeps it out.
Good length delivery on off, Sohail defends off the front foot.
Short outside off, Sohail cuts it towards point for a single.
Bowls a bouncer, Sohail does well to duck under it.
Full on middle, Sohail plays it to mid on.
Good length delivery on off, the left-hander defends off the back foot.
APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! Length delivery on middle, Sohail looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Probably height could have saved him.
Good length delivery outside off, Sohail lets it go.
Trent Boult is back on.
A little too wide outside off and it is that tempting, driving length. Imam though resists and makes a leave. End of a successful over.
Full and outside off, it is driven square on the off side for a run.
Back of a length on off, Sohail guides it to point.
A tough task awaits for Pakistan. A big onus lies on this current pair now. Imam and Haris need to dig in deep.

Drinks are on the field. Been New Zealand's morning so far. They first got the runs on the board rather quickly and have now bagged two wickets of Hafeez and Azhar. Southee and de Grandhomme provided the breakthroughs and the Kiwis are on the charge. This first session is an extended one, due to the Friday prayers, so there's plenty of time left for the visitors to get a wicket or two more. Haris Sohail is next in to bat, so he will have to stick it out with Imam and see this session out.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! There goes the centurion of the first innings, there goes Pakistan's stalwart and that too cheaply. Colin gets the better of him with a beauty! This is on a length and around off, it is angled into the batsman first. Ali plays the original trajectory. It though pitches and moves away enough to take the outside edge. Watling behind the stumps accepts an easy catch. The away side is ecstatic as it is right on top here. 8 wickets more for them to take and another 67.3 overs left in the day.
Another length ball around off, Azhar Ali defends it towards covers.
Length again around off, the batsman blocks it onto the ground.
Bowls full on off, Imam looks to drive but gets a bottom edge on this one and it goes just close to the stumps. He is lucky to survive.
Bowls a yorker, Imam easily digs it out.
Good length delivery on off, Imam defends off the back foot.
Short outside off, Imam shoulders his arms to this one.
Length delivery on leg, Azhar flicks it towards square leg for a single.
Good length delivery on off, Azhar defends off the front foot.
Length delivery on middle, Azhar looks to defend but gets it off the inner half of the bat. It goes towards fine leg for a single.
Consecutive leaves for Azhar. Good length delivery outside off, Azhar lets it go.
Good length delivery outside off, the batsman shoulders arms to this one.
Good length delivery outside off, Azhar offers no shot.
Full on off, Azhar defends off the front foot.
Full outside off, Azhar offers no shot.
Colin de Grandhomme is into the attack.
Short on off, Imam plays it to the off side.
Wide outside off, the left-hander offers no shot.
Good length delivery on off, the left-hander defends off the back foot.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Imam. Full outside off, Imam drives it through covers for a boundary.
FOUR! Short outside off, Imam cuts it through point for a boundary. Second boundary for Imam in this innings.
Full on middle, Azhar flicks it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen get three runs.
Shortish delivery pounded in, on the stumps, Imam rises on his feet and defends it down on the leg side.
Cutting back in, on a length, defended off the inner half in front of square leg.
Good length delivery in line of the stumps, blocked with a straight blade in response.
Another bumper, it's sharp and accurate on off, Imam arches back and just about manages to duck under it.
Short of a length just outside off, kept out from the back foot.
Starts off with a bouncer, takes Imam by surprise a bit but he does well to evade it.
Full in length outside off, driven to covers to end the over.
Too far down the leg side, Azhar attempts to flick it away but fails to do so.
Azhar Ali is the next batsman in.

OUT! Bowled 'em! The Professor is knocked out early in his last Test innings. A beauty from Southee to dismiss him. Absolute peach. Southee comes from wide of the crease and angles it in on off, it straightens up once more and this time it's enough to beat Hafeez's defense. It goes past the outside edge and knocks the bails over. An 18-year long career comes to a close. He walks back to a standing ovation from the crowd. Acknowledges their support and raises his bat in appreciation. He'd have liked to do more obviously, but he can be happy on the whole with the kind of career he's had.
Angling in at first and then straightens up off the seam, Hafeez is squared up a bit but he still manages to defend this a bit square on the off side.
Moving away this time, a length delivery around off, Hafeez pats it away to covers.
Marginally ahead of a length, quite close to off, Hafeez stays inside the crease and defends it down on the off side with soft hands.
The outswinger to finish things. Boult pitches it full and makes it go away, the batsman plays and misses.
Too full and too straight in line, Imam flicks it past the diving mid-wicket fielder. A couple of runs result this time.
FOUR! That's a good shot. Nice sound of the ball going off the bat. Some width offered outside off, Imam is on the back foot in a jiffy as he cuts this through point for a boundary.
Darts it on a length in the off stump channel, the left-hander shoulders his arms to it.

FOUR BYES! Bowls down the leg side, Imam still goes after it but does not connect. It goes behind where Watling dives to his right and gets a hand to it but could not stop it and it goes for a boundary.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Good length delivery on off, Hafeez keeps it out.
Good length delivery outside off, the batsman offers no shot.
Length delivery outside off, Hafeez offers no shot and it kept low on him.
Wide outside off, Hafeez lets it go.
Bowls wide outside off, Hafeez shoulders his arms to this one.
FOUR! Short of length delivery, Hafeez pulls it through square leg for a boundary. First boundary for Pakistan.
Sharp bumper just around off, it's quite accurate from Boult. Imam watches the ball and just about manages to evade it by arching back.
Cuts back in this time, from a good length, kept out solidly from within the crease.
Too far outside off, no chance the southpaw bothers himself with that.
On the fuller side of things once more, Imam stays right behind the line and blocks it back down the track.
Yorker fired in on the stumps, swinging away from the batsman, he brings his bat down in time and jams it out.
Shaping away from outside off, on a good length, Imam plants his front foot forward and leaves it alone.
Good length delivery on off, Hafeez blocks it well.
Wide outside off, Hafeez offers no shot.
Good length delivery on off, Hafeez defends off the back foot.
Wide outside off, the right-hander lets it go.
Good length delivery on off, Hafeez keeps it out.
Good length delivery outside off, Hafeez lets it go.
Length delivery on off, Imam plays it to the off side.
Bowls wide outside off, Imam easily offers no shot to this one.
BEATEN! Good length delivery outside off, Imam covers the line and the ball passes the bat very closely. Luckily he did not get an edge.
Length delivery on middle, the left-hander defends off the back foot.
Good length delivery outside off, Imam looks to defend but misses it and gets beaten on this one.
Good length delivery outside off, Imam shoulders his arms to this one.
Trent Boult will share the new ball from the other end.
Short outside off, Hafeez cuts it towards point. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Good length delivery outside off, the batsman lets it go.
Good length delivery on off, Hafeez defends off the front foot.

DROPPED! Full outside off, Hafeez looks to drive but gets an outside edge towards gully. Williamson there gets two hands to it but the ball bursts through and goes down towards third man for a couple. He may have reacted late. You though expect Williamson to catch that. However, a lucky reprieve for Hafeez in his last-ever Test innings. Can he make full use of it and play a majestic knock here? He would love to bow out in some style.
Bowls full on middle, Imam flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single. First runs for Pakistan.
Good length delivery outside off, Imam lets it go.
